q: Why does a primality test only need to try divisors up to √n?
options: If n = a × b with both a and b > √n, then a × b > n, so one factor must be ≤ √n
It's a heuristic that usually works
why: Factors come in pairs around √n. If none is found up to √n, there's none above it either.

q: You must answer 'is k prime?' for 100,000 different k values, all ≤ 10⁶. Best approach?
options: Build a sieve up to 10⁶ once, then O(1) lookups
why: One O(n log log n) sieve + O(1) per query beats 10⁵ × O(√k) trial divisions: a precompute-then-lookup trade-off.
